title: date-fns
description: Modern date utility library with tree-shaking.

data.text: date-fns provides 200+ functions for manipulating JavaScript dates with a functional programming style.

data.title: date-fns example

data.text: date-fns is a collection of pure functions that operate on native `Date` objects: `format`, `parseISO`, `addDays`, `differenceInDays`, `startOfMonth`. There is no mutable date object and no chained API, so each function is small and tree-shakeable.

data.title: Formatting, arithmetic, and comparison

data.text: date-fns works in the runtime time zone. When you need a specific zone, pairs with `date-fns-tz` provide `utcToZonedTime` and `zonedTimeToUtc`, and locale objects change month and day names. Note that a pair is now the supported path since date-fns v3 moved time-zone support out of the core.

data.title: Zoned conversion and localization
Interview angle: dates are not just formatting
data.text: The interview-worthy point is the storage decision: store timestamps as UTC (a `timestamptz` in the database), convert to a zone only for display, and never store a local time without its zone. date-fns can do the arithmetic and formatting, but the correctness comes from that discipline.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Functional API is easy to test.
